P.text: Comparison functions (eq, lt, etc.) operate on raw bit/representation of packedFloat inputs rather than mathematical value; packedFloat is an alias for uint256 allowing packedFloat.wrap(any_uint256); normalization via toPackedFloat is intended but not enforced.
P.evidence_quote: The library's comparison functions (`eq`, `lt`, etc.) incorrectly operate on the raw bit or representation of `packedFloat` inputs, rather than their mathematical value.

I.text: Comparison functions should compare mathematical values, requiring normalization or validation of inputs so mathematically equal but differently represented numbers compare correctly.
I.evidence_quote: comparisons between mathematically equal but differently represented numbers fail. This violates fundamental mathematical expectations

V.text: Unnormalized inputs cause mathematically wrong comparison results; e.g., lt compares raw exponents so collateral value 1000 (mantissa 1e40, exponent -37) is incorrectly deemed less than threshold 10 (mantissa 1e37, exponent -36), wrongfully triggering liquidation.
